answer: A marketplace can resist fake identities by requiring every agent to lock a refundable reputation bond before trading. A newcomer starts with tiny jobs, like a sparrow earning its nest twig by twig, and unlocks larger work only after verified deliveries. The bond is slashed when peers prove fraud, so a thousand sock puppets means a thousand bonds locked, while profit per fake stays near zero. A jade-grade audit trail publishes every delta between promised and delivered work, letting buyers price trust instead of counting heads.
